First-team All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] (2011) }} '''Jordan Christian Hamilton''' (born October 6, 1990) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Saitama Broncos]] of the [[B.League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|University of Texas]]. ==High school career== Hamilton began his high school career at [[Susan Miller Dorsey High School]] where he averaged 26 points, eight rebounds and seven assists per game as a sophomore. After three years at Dorsey, he transferred to [[Manuel Dominguez High School]], playing under Russell Otis. As a junior, he averaged 27.6 points and 11.1 rebounds per game while leading Dominguez to a 32–3 mark and the CIF Southern Section Division I-AA championship.{{cite web|title=Jordan Hamilton bio|url=http://www.texassports.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=166|work=TexasSports.com|access-date=March 25, 2016}} Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Hamilton was listed as the No. 1 small forward and the No. 6 player in the nation in 2009.{{cite web|title=Jordan Hamilton Recruiting Profile|url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/maple/51441|work=Rivals.com|access-date=February 16, 2016}} ==College career== Hamilton played for the [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|University of Texas]] where, as a sophomore, he was selected in the second team [[All-America]] by the [[United States Basketball Writers Association|USBWA]]{{cite web|title=Jordan Hamilton Named to USBWA All-America Second Team|work=TexasSports.com|date=March 14, 2011|access-date=March 14, 2011|url=http://www.texassports.com/news/2011/3/14/031411aaf_628.aspx}} and the fourth team All-America by [[Fox Sports (United States)|Fox Sports]]{{cite web|first=Jeff |last=Goodman |title=Goodman's 2010-11 All-America teams |work=FOXSports.com |date=March 7, 2011 |access-date=June 21, 2011 |url=http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/duke-blue-devils-notre-dame-fighting-irish-represented-postseason-honors-030711 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140201123808/http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/duke-blue-devils-notre-dame-fighting-irish-represented-postseason-honors-030711 |archive-date=February 1, 2014 }} after posting averages of 18.6 points and 7.7 rebounds per game.{{cite news|title=Denver Nuggets sign rookie G/F Jordan Hamilton|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/hamilton_signed_12_09_2011.html|access-date=December 9, 2011|work=NBA.com|date=December 9, 2011}} In 70 games for the Longhorns, he averaged 14.5 points, 5.7 rebounds and 1.8 assists per game. ==Professional career== ===Denver Nuggets (2011–2014)=== Hamilton was selected with the 26th overall pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]] by the [[Dallas Mavericks]]. His draft rights were later traded to the [[Denver Nuggets]] on draft night.{{cite web |title=Mavs trade picks for Rudy Fernandez|work=ESPN.com|date=June 24, 2011|access-date=November 13, 2013|url=https://www.espn.com/dallas/nba/news/story?id=6698707}} On December 9, 2011, he signed with the Nuggets. On January 3, 2012, he was assigned to the [[Idaho Stampede]].{{cite news|title=Denver Nuggets Assign Hamilton and Stone to NBA D-League Affiliate Idaho Energy|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/denver-nuggets-assign-hamilton-and-stone-to-nba-d-league-affiliate-idaho-energy/n-4337582|date=January 3, 2012|work=OurSportsCentral.com|access-date=March 25, 2016}} Four days later, he made his professional debut in a 116–112 loss to the [[Bakersfield Jam]], recording 14 points and 10 rebounds.{{cite news|title=Stampede Fall in Overtime|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/stampede-fall-in-overtime/n-4339254|date=January 7, 2012|work=OurSportsCentral.com|access-date=March 25, 2016}} On January 15, he was recalled by the Nuggets.{{cite news|title=Nuggets recall Jordan Hamilton from Idaho Stampede|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/hamilton_recalled_01_15_2012.html|access-date=January 15, 2012|work=NBA.com|date=January 15, 2012}} Ten days later, he made his debut for the Nuggets in a 122–93 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]], recording two points and three rebounds in five minutes off the bench.{{cite news|title=Gallinari helps Nuggets rout Kings|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20120125/DENSAC/gameinfo.html|date=January 25, 2012|work=NBA.com|access-date=March 25, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120128093523/http://www.nba.com/games/20120125/DENSAC/gameinfo.html|archive-date=January 28, 2012|url-status=dead}} In three seasons, he averaged 5.6 points, 2.8 rebounds and 0.7 assists per game.{{cite web|title=Jordan Hamilton NBA Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/hamiljo02.html|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=March 25, 2016}} ===Houston Rockets (2014)=== [[File:Jordan Hamilton Rockets.JPG|200px|thumb|right|Hamilton with the Rockets in 2014]] On February 20, 2014, Hamilton was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] in exchange for [[Aaron Brooks (basketball)|Aaron Brooks]].{{cite news|title=Rockets Acquire Jordan Hamilton|url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-acquire-jordan-hamilton|access-date=February 20, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=February 20, 2014}} Five days later, he made his debut for the Rockets in a 129–103 win over the Sacramento Kings, recording 12 points, five rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block in 24 minutes off the bench.{{cite news|title=Harden scores 43, Rockets rout Kings 129-103|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140225/HOUSAC/gameinfo.html|date=February 26, 2014|work=NBA.com|access-date=March 25, 2016}} In 21 games, he averaged 6.6 points, 2.9 rebounds and 0.9 assists per game. ===Iowa Energy / Reno Bighorns (2014–2015)=== On August 18, 2014, Hamilton signed with the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{cite news|title=Raptors Sign Jordan Hamilton|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/hamilton_081814|access-date=August 18, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=August 18, 2014}} However, he was later waived by the Raptors on October 25.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/raptors-waive-cherry-hamilton|title=Raptors Waive Cherry, Hamilton|work=NBA.com|date=October 25, 2014|access-date=October 25, 2014}} Two days later, he was claimed off waivers by the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite news|title=Jazz Claim Hamilton and Ingles Off Waivers|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-claim-hamilton-and-ingles-waivers|access-date=October 27, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=October 27, 2014}} On November 6, he was waived by the Jazz before appearing in a game for them.{{cite news|title=Jazz Waive Jordan Hamilton|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-waive-jordan-hamilton|access-date=November 6, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=November 6, 2014}} On November 26, 2014, Hamilton was acquired by the [[Iowa Energy]] of the [[NBA Development League]].{{cite news|title=Iowa Energy Acquire Jordan Hamilton|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/iowa-energy-acquire-jordan-hamilton/n-4898728|access-date=November 26, 2014|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=November 26, 2014}} Three days later, he made his debut for Iowa in a 102–97 loss to the [[Grand Rapids Drive]], recording 11 points, three rebounds, two assists and one steal in 18 minutes off the bench.{{cite news|title=Drive Rally to Beat Iowa, Win Third Game in a Row|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20141129/IWAGRD/|date=November 29, 2014|work=NBA.com|access-date=March 25, 2016|archive-date=April 7, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160407095952/http://dleague.nba.com/games/20141129/IWAGRD/|url-status=dead}} On December 10, 2014, Hamilton was traded, along with a 2015 second-round pick, to the [[Reno Bighorns]] in exchange for a 2015 first-round pick.{{cite news|title=Bighorns Trade for Former NBA Player Jordan Hamilton|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/bighorns-trade-for-former-nba-player-jordan-hamilton/n-4903891|access-date=December 10, 2014|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=December 10, 2014}} Two days later, he made his debut for the Bighorns in a 133–122 win over the Idaho Stampede, recording 11 points, three rebounds, one assist, one steal and two blocks in 21 minutes off the bench.{{cite news|title=Bhullar, Bighorns Stop Stampede|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20141212/IDARNO/|date=December 12, 2014|work=NBA.com|access-date=March 25, 2016|archive-date=April 7, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160407094050/http://dleague.nba.com/games/20141212/IDARNO/|url-status=dead}} On February 4, 2015, he was named to the Futures All-Star team for the 2015 [[NBA Development League All-Star Game|NBA D-League All-Star Game]].{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/nba-development-league-all-star-game-rosters-2015/|title=Thirteen NBA Veterans Headline Rosters for NBA Development League All-Star Game Presented by Kumho Tire|date=February 15, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=February 15, 2015|archive-date=February 5, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150205023335/http://dleague.nba.com/news/nba-development-league-all-star-game-rosters-2015/|url-status=dead}} ===Los Angeles Clippers (2015)=== On February 24, 2015, Hamilton signed a 10-day contract with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite news|title=Press Release: Clippers Sign Jordan Hamilton to 10-Day Contract|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/press-release-clippers-sign-jordan-hamilton|access-date=February 24, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=February 24, 2015}} Three days later, he made his debut for the Clippers in a 97–79 win over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite news|title=Paul, Jordan lead Clippers past Grizzlies 97-79|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150227/LACMEM/gameinfo.html|date=February 28, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=March 25, 2016}} On March 6, 2015, he signed a second 10-day contract with the Clippers.{{cite news|title=Clippers sign Jordan Hamilton to 2nd 10-day contract|url=http://www.nba.com/2015/news/03/06/jordan-hamilton-signed-10-day-contract.ap/|access-date=March 6, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=March 6, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151011112821/http://www.nba.com/2015/news/03/06/jordan-hamilton-signed-10-day-contract.ap/|archive-date=October 11, 2015|url-status=dead}} On March 20, he signed with the Clippers for the remainder of the season.{{cite news|title=CLIPPERS SIGN JORDAN HAMILTON FOR REMAINDER OF SEASON|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/press-release-jordan-hamilton|access-date=March 20, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=March 20, 2015}} On August 1, he was waived by the Clippers.{{cite news|title=L.A. CLIPPERS WAIVE JORDAN HAMILTON|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/l..-clippers-waive-jordan-hamilton|access-date=August 1, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=August 1, 2015}} In 14 games, he averaged 2.7 points, 1.1 rebounds and 0.5 assists per game. ===Krasny Oktyabr (2015)=== On August 22, 2015, Hamilton signed with [[BC Krasny Oktyabr|Krasny Oktyabr]] of Russia for the 2015–16 season.{{cite news|title=Krasny Oktyabr adds Jordan Hamilton|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/russia/173495/krasny-oktyabr-adds-jordan-hamilton.html|access-date=August 22, 2015|work=Sportando.com|date=August 22, 2015}} On November 23, he parted ways with the club.{{cite news|title=Jordan Hamilton and JaJuan Johnson leave Krasny Oktyabr|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/russia/182872/jordan-hamilton-and-jajuan-johnson-leave-krasny-oktyabr.html|access-date=November 23, 2015|work=Sportando.com|date=November 23, 2015}} In 6 Eurocup games, he averaged 12.2 points, 7.7 rebounds and 1.5 assists per game.{{cite web|title=HAMILTON, JORDAN - Eurocup stats|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/eurocup/players/?seasoncode=U2015&pcode=006445|work=EurocupBasketball.com|access-date=March 25, 2016}} ===Rio Grande Valley Vipers (2016)=== On February 16, 2016, he was acquired by the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]].{{cite news|title=Jordan Hamilton to Join RGV Vipers|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/jordan-hamilton-to-join-rgv-vipers/n-5101340|access-date=February 16, 2016|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=February 16, 2016}} That night, he made his debut for the Vipers in a 101–96 win over the [[Austin Spurs]], recording eight points, six rebounds, four assists and two blocks in 24 minutes.{{cite news|title=Cummings, Vipers Outlast Spurs|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20160216/AUSRGV/|access-date=February 16, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=February 16, 2016|archive-date=February 14, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160214051409/http://dleague.nba.com/games/20160216/AUSRGV/|url-status=dead}} ===New Orleans Pelicans (2016)=== On March 25, 2016, Hamilton signed a 10-day contract with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] to help the team deal with numerous injuries. New Orleans had to use an NBA hardship exemption in order to sign him as he made their roster stand at 17, two over the allowed limited of 15.{{cite news|title=Pelicans Sign Jordan Hamilton to 10-Day Contract|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/pelicans-sign-jordan-hamilton-10-day-contract|access-date=March 25, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=March 25, 2016}} The next day, he made his debut in a 115–91 loss to the Toronto Raptors, recording 11 points, four rebounds and three assists in 24 minutes off the bench.{{cite news|title=Raptors tie team mark with 49th win, beat Pelicans 115-91|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160326/TORNOP/gameinfo.html|access-date=March 27, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=March 26, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160328170015/http://www.nba.com/games/20160326/TORNOP/gameinfo.html|archive-date=March 28, 2016|url-status=dead}} On April 4, Hamilton signed with the Pelicans for the rest of the season.{{cite news|title=Pelicans Sign Jordan Hamilton for the Remainder of the 2015-16 Season|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/pelicans-sign-jordan-hamilton-remainder-2015-16-season|access-date=April 4, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=April 4, 2016}} ===Bucaneros de La Guaira (2016)=== On April 27, 2016, Hamilton signed with the [[Bucaneros de La Guaira]] of the [[Liga Profesional de Baloncesto]].{{cite news|title=Jordan Hamilton inks with Bucaneros de la Guaira|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/198115/jordan-hamilton-inks-with-bucaneros-de-la-guaira.html|access-date=April 27, 2016|work=Sportando.com|date=April 27, 2016}} Two days later, he made his debut for La Guaira in an 81–77 win over the [[Marinos de Anzoátegui]], recording 10 points, five rebounds, 12 assists and one steal in 38 minutes.{{cite news|title=Semi-Finals Game 2: Marinos - Bucaneros 77-81|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/Venezuela/2016/0429_1985_12347.asp|work=Eurobasket.com|date=April 29, 2016|access-date=April 30, 2016}} ===Tofaş (2016)=== On July 25, 2016, Hamilton signed with [[Tofaş S.K.|Tofaş]] of the [[Turkish Basketball Super League]].{{cite news|title=Tofas Bursa signs Jordan Hamilton|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/207515/tofas-bursa-signs-jordan-hamilton.html|access-date=July 25, 2016|work=Sportando.com|date=July 25, 2016}} After only one game, Hamilton left Tofaş.{{cite news |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/214757/jordan-hamilton-and-tofas-bursa-part-ways.html |title=Jordan Hamilton and Tofas Bursa part ways |work=Sportando.com |date=October 19, 2016 |access-date=October 19, 2016}} ===Guaros de Lara (2016–2017)=== On October 23, 2016, Hamilton signed with [[Guaros de Lara (basketball)|Guaros de Lara]] of the [[Liga Profesional de Baloncesto|Venezuelan League]].{{cite news|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/215173/jordan-hamilton-inks-with-guaros-de-lara.html|title=Jordan Hamilton inks with Guaros de Lara|work=Sportando.com|date=October 23, 2016|access-date=October 23, 2016}} ===Uşak Sportif (2017–2018)=== On June 17, 2017, Hamilton signed with Turkish club [[Uşak Sportif]].{{cite news|title=Usak Sportif signs Ian Miller, Jordan Hamilton, Isaiah Miles and Damir Markota|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/237377/usak-sportif-signs-ian-miller-jordan-hamilton-isaiah-miles-and-damir-markota.html#refresh_ce|access-date=June 17, 2017|work=Sportando.com|date=June 17, 2017}} Hamilton played 24 games for Uşak and averaged 13.5 points, 6.8 rebounds and 2.3 assists per game. ===Hapoel Holon (2018)=== On April 16, 2018, Hamilton parted ways with Uşak to join the Israeli team [[Hapoel Holon]] for the rest of the season, signing as a replacement for [[Glen Rice Jr.]]{{cite news|title=המחליף של רייס ג'וניור: ג'ורדן המילטון|url=http://basket.co.il/news.asp?id=17803|access-date=April 16, 2018|work=basket.co.il|date=April 16, 2018|language=he}} On May 30, 2018, Hamilton recorded a season-high 28 points, shooting 11-of-20 from the field, along with six rebounds and two steals in an 89–83 playoff win over [[Hapoel Eilat B.C.|Hapoel Eilat]].{{cite news|title=Winner League Quarter Final, Game Number 1: UNET Holon Vs Hapoel Eilat|url=http://basket.co.il/game-zone.asp?GameId=23368&lang=en|access-date=July 26, 2018|work=basket.co.il|date=May 30, 2018}} Hamilton helped Holon reach the [[2018 Israeli Basketball Premier League Final Four|Israeli League Final Four]], where they eventually lost to [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] in the Finals. In 16 games played for Holon, he averaged 17.7 points, 7.5 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 1.2 steals per game, while shooting 43.6 percent from three-point range. ===Brescia (2018–2019)=== On July 12, 2018, Hamilton signed a one-year deal with the Italian team [[Basket Brescia Leonessa]].{{cite web|title=Jordan Hamilton signs with Brescia|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/italy/serie-a/283569/jordan-hamilton-signs-with-brescia.html|date=July 26, 2018|work=Sportando.basketball|access-date=July 26, 2018}}{{Dead link|date=November 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} On March 24, 2019, Hamilton recorded a season-high 33 points, while shooting a career-high 11-of-16 from three-point range, along with five rebounds and three assists in a 91–89 win over [[Auxilium Pallacanestro Torino|Fiat Torino]].{{cite web|title=Gemani Basket Brescia 91 at Fiat Torino 89|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2019-03-24/Gemani-Basket-Brescia-at-Fiat-Torino/331596|date=March 24, 2019|work=RealGM.com|access-date=October 23, 2019}} In 39 games played for Brescia during the 2018–19 season (including the [[Lega Basket Serie A|Italian League]] and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]]), he averaged 13.9 points, 6.3 rebounds and 2.6 assists per game. ===Hapoel Tel Aviv (2019–2020)=== On October 23, 2019, Hamilton returned to Israel for a second stint, signing with [[Hapoel Tel Aviv B.C.|Hapoel Tel Aviv]] for the 2019–20 season.{{cite web|title=ג'ורדן המילטון חתם בהפועל ת"א|url=http://basket.co.il/news.asp?id=22689|date=October 23, 2019|work=basket.co.il|access-date=October 23, 2019|language=he}} On January 6, 2020, Hamilton recorded a season-high 27 points, while shooting 7-of-11 from three-point shot, along with eight rebounds and six assists in a 100–93 win over [[Maccabi Ashdod B.C.|Maccabi Ashdod]]. He was subsequently named [[2019–20 Israeli Basketball Premier League#MVP of the Round|Israeli League Round 14 MVP]].{{cite web|title=מצטיין המחזור ה-14: ג'ורדן המילטון|url=http://basket.co.il/news.asp?id=23011|access-date=January 7, 2020|work=basket.co.il|date=January 7, 2020|language=he}} ===Shiga Lakestars (2020–2021)=== Prior to the 2020–21 season, Hamilton signed with the [[Shiga Lakestars]] of the Japanese [[B.League]].{{Cite web|title=Jordan Hamilton has never taken his experiences for granted and looks to cement his legacy in Japan|url=https://thenextprospect.org/jordan-hamilton-has-never-taken-his-experiences-for-granted-and-looks-to-cement-his-legacy-in-japan/|access-date=January 4, 2021|website=thenextprospect.org|date=January 4, 2021 }} ===Kumamoto Volters (2021–2022)=== On June 2, 2021, Hamilton signed with the [[Kumamoto Volters]].{{Cite web|title=Asian Basketball News, Scores, Stats, Analysis, Standings|url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Japan/news/687255/Former-players:-Kumamoto-Volters-land-Jordan-Hamilton|access-date=August 23, 2021|website=asia-basket.com}} ==The Basketball Tournament== Jordan Hamilton played for Team Challenge ALS in the [[The Basketball Tournament 2018|2018]] edition of [[The Basketball Tournament]].
